s.t: A king and queen lived in a castle.
s.fr: Un roi et une reine vivaient dans un château.

s.t: For many years, they had no child.
s.fr: Pendant de nombreuses années, ils n’avaient pas d’enfant.

s.t: The queen wanted a child of her own.
s.fr: La reine voulait un enfant à elle.

s.t: She wanted white skin, red lips, and black hair for the baby.
s.fr: Elle voulait une peau blanche, des lèvres rouges, et des cheveux noirs pour le bébé.

s.t: Soon the queen had a baby daughter.
s.fr: Bientôt, la reine eut une fille bébé.

s.t: The baby had white skin, red lips, and black hair.
s.fr: Le bébé avait une peau blanche, des lèvres rouges, et des cheveux noirs.

s.t: The king and queen called her Snow White.
s.fr: Le roi et la reine l’appelèrent Blanche-Neige.

paras.summary: A king and queen live in a castle with many people on the land of their kingdom, but for years they have no child; the queen wants a baby with white skin, red lips, and black hair, and soon has a baby daughter just as she wanted, so they call her Snow White, and servants help care for her.

s.t: One morning, the queen fell sick.
s.fr: Un matin, la reine tomba malade.

s.t: She died when Snow White was still a baby.
s.fr: Elle mourut quand Blanche-Neige était encore un bébé.

s.t: The king was alone with his baby daughter.
s.fr: Le roi était seul avec sa fille bébé.

s.t: For some years, he raised her alone.
s.fr: Pendant quelques années, il l’éleva seul.

paras.summary: But the queen falls sick and dies when Snow White is still a baby, leaving the king alone with his baby daughter, whom he loves and raises alone for some years.

s.t: When Snow White was still young, the king married again.
s.fr: Quand Blanche-Neige était encore jeune, le roi se maria de nouveau.

s.t: His new wife, the queen, was beautiful.
s.fr: Sa nouvelle femme, la reine, était belle.

s.t: The king told Snow White to love the new queen.
s.fr: Le roi dit à Blanche-Neige d’aimer la nouvelle reine.

s.t: Snow White grew up in the castle.
s.fr: Blanche-Neige grandit dans le château.

s.t: The new queen owned a magic mirror.
s.fr: La nouvelle reine possédait un miroir magique.

s.t: The mirror could answer the queen.
s.fr: Le miroir pouvait répondre à la reine.

s.t: Every morning, the queen stood before the mirror.
s.fr: Chaque matin, la reine se plaçait devant le miroir.

paras.summary: When Snow White is still young, the king marries a beautiful new queen and tells Snow White to love her; Snow White grows up in the castle, where the new queen owns a magic mirror that can answer her, and every morning she stands before it.

s.t: "Mirror, mirror, who is the fairest in the land?" she asked.
s.fr: « Miroir, miroir, qui est la plus belle du pays ? » dit-elle.

s.t: "You are the fairest in the land," the mirror answered.
s.fr: « Vous êtes la plus belle du pays, » répondit le miroir.

s.t: The queen smiled at this answer.
s.fr: La reine sourit à cette réponse.

paras.summary: Every morning the queen asks the mirror who is the fairest in the land, and it always gives the same answer; many servants work in the castle and care for Snow White, but the people never see the mirror.

s.t: Years passed, and Snow White grew into a kind young woman.
s.fr: Les années passèrent, et Blanche-Neige devint une jeune femme gentille.

s.t: She still had white skin, red lips, and black hair.
s.fr: Elle avait encore la peau blanche, les lèvres rouges, et les cheveux noirs.

s.t: The people of the land loved Snow White.
s.fr: Les gens du pays aimaient Blanche-Neige.

paras.summary: Years pass, and Snow White grows into a kind young woman who still has white skin, red lips, and black hair; the people of the land love her, and the queen is still beautiful too.

s.t: One morning, the queen stood before her mirror again.
s.fr: Un matin, la reine se plaça devant son miroir de nouveau.

s.t: This time, the mirror gave a new answer.
s.fr: Cette fois, le miroir donna une nouvelle réponse.

s.t: "Snow White is the fairest in the land now," said the mirror.
s.fr: « Blanche-Neige est la plus belle du pays maintenant, » dit le miroir.

paras.summary: One morning the queen asks her mirror again who is the fairest in the land, and this time it gives a new answer: Snow White is the fairest now.

s.t: Her face went red at this answer.
s.fr: Son visage devint rouge à cette réponse.

s.t: "Snow White will not be the fairest," she said.
s.fr: « Blanche-Neige ne sera pas la plus belle, » dit-elle.

s.t: The queen wanted to be the fairest in the land.
s.fr: La reine voulait être la plus belle du pays.

s.t: The queen wanted Snow White gone from the king's castle.
s.fr: La reine voulait Blanche-Neige loin du château du roi.

s.t: She called for her huntsman at the castle.
s.fr: Elle appela son chasseur au château.

paras.summary: The queen says nothing, her face goes red, and she says Snow White will not be the fairest, for she wants to be the fairest in the land; wanting Snow White gone from the castle, she calls for her huntsman.

s.t: The huntsman came before the queen.
s.fr: Le chasseur vint devant la reine.

s.t: "Take Snow White into the forest," said the queen.
s.fr: « Emmène Blanche-Neige dans la forêt, » dit la reine.

s.t: "Kill her there, and bring me her heart," she said.
s.fr: « Tue-la là-bas, et apporte-moi son cœur, » dit-elle.

s.t: The huntsman did not want to do this.
s.fr: Le chasseur ne voulait pas faire cela.

s.t: He looked at the queen and said nothing.
s.fr: Il regarda la reine et ne dit rien.

s.t: But he did what the queen asked.
s.fr: Mais il fit ce que la reine demandait.

paras.summary: The mirror still gives the same answer every morning, so the huntsman is called before the queen, who orders him to take Snow White into the forest, kill her, and bring back her heart, smiling at him; he does not want to do this, and he says nothing.

s.t: He took Snow White into the forest.
s.fr: Il emmena Blanche-Neige dans la forêt.

s.t: Snow White believed the huntsman.
s.fr: Blanche-Neige crut le chasseur.

s.t: She did not know of the queen's plan.
s.fr: Elle ne savait pas le plan de la reine.

s.t: Birds sang in the tall trees around them.
s.fr: Des oiseaux chantaient dans les grands arbres autour d’eux.

s.t: The huntsman stopped in the forest.
s.fr: Le chasseur s’arrêta dans la forêt.

s.t: He raised his knife.
s.fr: Il leva son couteau.

paras.summary: But he does as the queen asks and leads Snow White into the forest, where she believes him and knows nothing of the queen's plan; as birds sing around them, the huntsman stops and raises his knife.

s.t: Snow White saw the knife and moved back.
s.fr: Blanche-Neige vit le couteau et recula.

s.t: "Do not kill me," she said.
s.fr: « Ne me tuez pas, » dit-elle.

s.t: "I will run away and never come back," she said.
s.fr: « Je m’enfuirai et ne reviendrai jamais, » dit-elle.

s.t: The huntsman looked at her kind face.
s.fr: Le chasseur regarda son visage doux.

s.t: He could not kill her with the knife.
s.fr: Il ne pouvait pas la tuer avec le couteau.

s.t: "Run, and never come back to the castle," he said.
s.fr: « Cours, et ne reviens jamais au château, » dit-il.

s.t: Snow White ran into the forest alone.
s.fr: Blanche-Neige courut dans la forêt seule.

paras.summary: Snow White begs the huntsman not to kill her and promises to run away and never come back; he cannot do it, so he tells her to run and never come back, and she runs alone into the forest as the birds still sing around her.

s.t: The huntsman wanted a heart for the queen.
s.fr: Le chasseur voulait un cœur pour la reine.

s.t: He found a deer in the forest.
s.fr: Il trouva un cerf dans la forêt.

s.t: The huntsman killed the deer, not Snow White.
s.fr: Le chasseur tua le cerf, pas Blanche-Neige.

s.t: He went back to the castle in the evening.
s.fr: Il retourna au château le soir.

s.t: He carried the deer's heart to the queen.
s.fr: Il porta le cœur du cerf à la reine.

s.t: "Here is Snow White's heart," he told the queen.
s.fr: « Voici le cœur de Blanche-Neige, » dit-il à la reine.

s.t: The queen believed Snow White was dead, and she smiled.
s.fr: La reine crut que Blanche-Neige était morte, et elle sourit.

paras.summary: The huntsman, wanting a heart for the queen, finds and kills a deer in her place, goes back to the castle in the evening, and tells the queen it is Snow White's heart; the queen believes Snow White is dead, and she smiles.

s.t: Snow White walked through the forest alone.
s.fr: Blanche-Neige marcha à travers la forêt seule.

s.t: But no huntsman was there to help her.
s.fr: Mais aucun chasseur n’était là pour l’aider.

s.t: Tall trees stood all around her in the forest.
s.fr: De grands arbres se dressaient tout autour d’elle dans la forêt.

paras.summary: Snow White walks through the forest alone, away from the queen and the castle now, but with no huntsman there to help her, past tall trees standing all around.

s.t: Animals moved in the trees.
s.fr: Des animaux bougeaient dans les arbres.

s.t: But the animals of the forest did not hurt her.
s.fr: Mais les animaux de la forêt ne la blessèrent pas.

s.t: Some animals walked near her in the trees.
s.fr: Certains animaux marchèrent près d’elle dans les arbres.

s.t: Snow White ate nothing in the forest.
s.fr: Blanche-Neige ne mangea rien dans la forêt.

paras.summary: Animals move in the trees but do not hurt her, and some walk near her; she eats nothing in the forest and wants to see people again.

s.t: Evening came, and the forest was black.
s.fr: Le soir vint, et la forêt était noire.

s.t: It was black all around her now.
s.fr: Il faisait noir tout autour d’elle maintenant.

s.t: Snow White found no house and no bed there.
s.fr: Blanche-Neige ne trouva ni maison ni lit là.

s.t: She walked on, and the morning came.
s.fr: Elle continua à marcher, et le matin arriva.

s.t: She saw the door of a small cottage in the trees.
s.fr: Elle vit la porte d’une petite chaumière dans les arbres.

paras.summary: Evening comes and the forest is black all around her, and she finds no house and no bed there; she walks on, and in the morning she sees the door of a small cottage in the trees.

s.t: Snow White walked up to the small cottage.
s.fr: Blanche-Neige s’approcha de la petite chaumière.

s.t: Birds sang all around her in the morning.
s.fr: Des oiseaux chantaient tout autour d’elle le matin.

paras.summary: Snow White walks up to a small cottage that stands alone in the forest, with birds singing all around her in the morning, while the queen is away in her castle.

s.t: Snow White called at the door.
s.fr: Blanche-Neige frappa à la porte.

s.t: No one answered the door of the cottage.
s.fr: Personne ne répondit à la porte de la chaumière.

s.t: Snow White opened the door and looked inside.
s.fr: Blanche-Neige ouvrit la porte et regarda à l’intérieur.

s.t: She saw a small table with seven small plates.
s.fr: Elle vit une petite table avec sept petites assiettes.

s.t: She ate a little food from all seven small plates.
s.fr: Elle mangea un peu de nourriture dans chacune des sept petites assiettes.

paras.summary: Snow White calls at the door, but no one answers and no one is home, so she opens the door and looks inside, finding a small table with seven small plates, and she eats a little food from all seven.

s.t: Upstairs, she found seven small beds.
s.fr: À l’étage, elle trouva sept petits lits.

s.t: Snow White was tired.
s.fr: Blanche-Neige était fatiguée.

s.t: She lay down on the smallest bed.
s.fr: Elle s’allongea sur le plus petit lit.

s.t: Soon Snow White fell asleep.
s.fr: Bientôt Blanche-Neige s’endormit.

paras.summary: Upstairs, she finds seven small beds; tired, she lies down on the smallest bed and soon falls asleep.

s.t: That evening, seven dwarfs came home from the mine.
s.fr: Ce soir-là, sept nains rentrèrent chez eux depuis la mine.

s.t: They found their small door open.
s.fr: Ils trouvèrent leur petite porte ouverte.

s.t: They found food gone from their small plates.
s.fr: Ils trouvèrent la nourriture disparue de leurs petites assiettes.

s.t: They found Snow White asleep upstairs.
s.fr: Ils trouvèrent Blanche-Neige endormie en haut.

s.t: Snow White woke and saw the seven dwarfs.
s.fr: Blanche-Neige se réveilla et vit les sept nains.

s.t: She told them about the queen and the huntsman.
s.fr: Elle leur parla de la reine et du chasseur.

paras.summary: That evening, seven dwarfs come home from the mine and find their door open, food gone from their plates, and Snow White asleep upstairs; she wakes and tells them about the queen and the huntsman, so the dwarfs now know about the queen and her mirror.

s.t: "Stay here with us," said the oldest dwarf.
s.fr: « Reste ici avec nous, » dit le plus vieux nain.

s.t: "Keep house for us when we work," he said.
s.fr: « Tiens la maison pour nous quand nous travaillons, » dit-il.

s.t: There was food and a bed for Snow White.
s.fr: Il y avait de la nourriture et un lit pour Blanche-Neige.

s.t: The dwarfs wanted Snow White to stay with them.
s.fr: Les nains voulaient que Blanche-Neige reste avec eux.

s.t: Snow White said she wanted to stay.
s.fr: Blanche-Neige dit qu’elle voulait rester.

s.t: She kept the small house for them.
s.fr: Elle entretint la petite maison pour eux.

s.t: Snow White made food for them in the morning.
s.fr: Blanche-Neige préparait de la nourriture pour eux le matin.

s.t: "Never open the door to a stranger," the dwarfs warned.
s.fr: « N’ouvrez jamais la porte à un étranger, » avertirent les nains.

paras.summary: The oldest dwarf offers to let her stay and keep house when they work, and there is food and a bed for her; the dwarfs want her to stay and she says she wants to stay, so she keeps their small house and makes food for them in the morning, and they warn her never to open the door to a stranger.

s.t: The queen's mirror said Snow White was still alive.
s.fr: Le miroir de la reine dit que Blanche-Neige était encore vivante.

s.t: She disguised herself as an old woman.
s.fr: Elle se déguisa en vieille femme.

s.t: She carried pretty laces in a basket to the cottage.
s.fr: Elle porta de jolis lacets dans un panier jusqu’à la chaumière.

s.t: The seven dwarfs were still away at the mine in the forest.
s.fr: Les sept nains étaient encore partis à la mine dans la forêt.

s.t: Snow White did not know the old woman at the door.
s.fr: Blanche-Neige ne connaissait pas la vieille femme à la porte.

s.t: Snow White opened the cottage door for the old woman.
s.fr: Blanche-Neige ouvrit la porte de la chaumière à la vieille femme.

s.t: "I have pretty laces for you," said the old woman.
s.fr: « J’ai de jolis lacets pour vous, » dit la vieille femme.

s.t: The old woman wanted to hurt Snow White with the laces.
s.fr: La vieille femme voulait blesser Blanche-Neige avec les lacets.

paras.summary: The queen's mirror says Snow White is still alive, so she disguises herself as an old woman, and carries pretty laces in a basket to the cottage while the seven dwarfs are away at the mine; Snow White, not knowing the old woman, opens the door for her, and the old woman means to hurt her.

s.t: The old woman pulled the dress laces too tight at the cottage.
s.fr: La vieille femme serra les lacets de la robe trop fort à la chaumière.

s.t: Snow White could not breathe, and she fell to the floor.
s.fr: Blanche-Neige ne pouvait pas respirer, et elle tomba sur le sol.

s.t: That evening, the dwarfs returned and found Snow White on the floor.
s.fr: Ce soir-là, les nains revinrent et trouvèrent Blanche-Neige sur le sol.

s.t: "Snow White's laces are too tight for the dress," said one dwarf.
s.fr: « Les lacets de Blanche-Neige sont trop serrés pour la robe, » dit un nain.

s.t: The dwarfs cut the tight laces from the dress.
s.fr: Les nains coupèrent les lacets serrés de la robe.

s.t: Snow White could breathe again in the small cottage.
s.fr: Blanche-Neige put respirer de nouveau dans la petite chaumière.

s.t: "Never open the door to anyone," the dwarfs warned.
s.fr: « N’ouvrez jamais la porte à personne, » avertirent les nains.

paras.summary: The old woman pulls the dress laces too tight, and Snow White falls to the floor unable to breathe; that evening the dwarfs return, find her, cut the tight laces from the dress, and she can breathe again, so they warn her never to open the door to anyone.

s.t: The queen learned that Snow White was still alive.
s.fr: La reine apprit que Blanche-Neige était encore vivante.

s.t: She made a poisoned comb and disguised herself again.
s.fr: Elle fabriqua un peigne empoisonné et se déguisa de nouveau.

s.t: She carried the comb in a basket to the cottage.
s.fr: Elle porta le peigne dans un panier jusqu’à la chaumière.

s.t: Snow White remembered the dwarfs and did not open the door.
s.fr: Blanche-Neige se souvint des nains et n’ouvrit pas la porte.

paras.summary: The queen learns that Snow White is still alive, makes a poisoned comb, disguises herself again, and carries it to the cottage, but this time Snow White remembers the dwarfs and does not open the door.

s.t: "Look at this pretty comb," said the old woman.
s.fr: « Regardez ce joli peigne, » dit-elle, la vieille femme.

s.t: Snow White looked through the window at the comb.
s.fr: Blanche-Neige regarda le peigne à travers la fenêtre.

s.t: She opened the door at the cottage just a little.
s.fr: Elle ouvrit la porte de la chaumière juste un peu.

s.t: The old woman ran the comb through Snow White's hair.
s.fr: La vieille femme passa le peigne dans les cheveux de Blanche-Neige.

s.t: The poison in the comb worked, and she fell to the floor.
s.fr: Le poison dans le peigne agit, et elle tomba sur le sol.

paras.summary: The old woman calls out with the pretty comb, and Snow White, looking through the window, opens the door just a little; the old woman means to hurt her again and combs the poison into her hair, and she falls down.

s.t: That evening, the dwarfs returned and found Snow White on the floor.
s.fr: Ce soir-là, les nains revinrent et trouvèrent Blanche-Neige sur le sol.

s.t: "There is a comb in Snow White's hair," said one dwarf.
s.fr: « Il y a un peigne dans les cheveux de Blanche-Neige, » dit un nain.

s.t: They pulled out the poisoned comb from her hair.
s.fr: Ils retirèrent le peigne empoisonné de ses cheveux.

s.t: Snow White woke up again in the cottage.
s.fr: Blanche-Neige se réveilla encore dans la chaumière.

s.t: "Do not open the door, not even a little," the dwarfs warned.
s.fr: « N’ouvrez pas la porte, pas même un peu, » avertirent les nains.

paras.summary: That evening the dwarfs return, find her, pull out the poisoned comb, and she wakes up again; this time they warn her not to open the door even a little.

s.t: The queen learned that Snow White was still alive.
s.fr: La reine apprit que Blanche-Neige était encore en vie.

s.t: This time, she made a poisoned apple in her castle.
s.fr: Cette fois, elle prépara une pomme empoisonnée dans son château.

s.t: One half of the apple was red, with poison inside.
s.fr: Une moitié de la pomme était rouge, avec du poison à l’intérieur.

s.t: The queen disguised herself again to bring the apple.
s.fr: La reine se déguisa encore pour apporter la pomme.

s.t: She carried the apple in a basket to the cottage.
s.fr: Elle porta la pomme dans un panier jusqu’à la chaumière.

s.t: Snow White would not open the door at all this time.
s.fr: Blanche-Neige ne voulut pas du tout ouvrir la porte cette fois.

paras.summary: The queen learns that Snow White is still alive and makes a poisoned apple herself, disguising herself again, but Snow White will not open the door at all this time.

s.t: "Take this apple," said the old woman at the window.
s.fr: « Prenez cette pomme, » dit-elle la vieille femme à la fenêtre.

s.t: "I want no apple from a stranger," said Snow White.
s.fr: « Je ne veux pas de pomme d’une étrangère, » dit Blanche-Neige.

s.t: The old woman cut the apple in half at the cottage.
s.fr: La vieille femme coupa la pomme en deux à la chaumière.

s.t: She ate the white half of the apple herself.
s.fr: Elle mangea elle-même la moitié blanche de la pomme.

s.t: "Look, it is safe to eat," said the old woman.
s.fr: « Regardez, c’est sans danger à manger, » dit la vieille femme.

paras.summary: The old woman offers an apple at the window, but Snow White wants none from a stranger, so the old woman cuts the apple in half and eats the white half herself to show it is safe.

s.t: Snow White believed the old woman's apple was safe.
s.fr: Blanche-Neige crut que la pomme de la vieille femme était sans danger.

s.t: She opened the cottage door to the old woman.
s.fr: Elle ouvrit la porte de la chaumière à la vieille femme.

s.t: Snow White took the red half and bit into it.
s.fr: Blanche-Neige prit la moitié rouge et y mordit.

s.t: She fell to the floor of the cottage.
s.fr: Elle tomba sur le sol de la chaumière.

paras.summary: Snow White believes the apple is safe now, opens the door to the old woman, takes the red half, bites into it, and falls to the floor.

s.t: That evening, the seven dwarfs returned home again.
s.fr: Ce soir-là, les sept nains rentrèrent de nouveau chez eux.

s.t: They found Snow White on the floor.
s.fr: Ils trouvèrent Blanche-Neige sur le sol.

s.t: This time, it was not the laces, not the comb.
s.fr: Cette fois, ce n’était pas les lacets, pas le peigne.

s.t: The dwarfs could not wake Snow White again.
s.fr: Les nains ne pouvaient pas réveiller Blanche-Neige encore.

s.t: They believed Snow White had died, and the seven dwarfs were sad.
s.fr: Ils croyaient que Blanche-Neige était morte, et les sept nains étaient tristes.

s.t: But Snow White still did not look dead.
s.fr: Mais Blanche-Neige n’avait toujours pas l’air morte.

paras.summary: That evening the dwarfs return, find Snow White on the floor with no laces and no comb to blame this time, and cannot wake her, so they believe she has died, and they are sad.

s.t: The dwarfs did not want to bury Snow White.
s.fr: Les nains ne voulaient pas enterrer Blanche-Neige.

s.t: They made a coffin of glass for Snow White.
s.fr: Ils fabriquèrent un cercueil de verre pour Blanche-Neige.

s.t: The dwarfs put Snow White inside the glass coffin.
s.fr: Les nains placèrent Blanche-Neige dans le cercueil de verre.

s.t: They carried the glass coffin to a hill in the forest.
s.fr: Ils portèrent le cercueil de verre jusqu’à une colline dans la forêt.

paras.summary: But Snow White does not look dead, so the dwarfs will not bury her; instead they make a coffin of glass, put her inside it, and carry it to a hill in the forest.

s.t: Birds and animals came to the hill to see Snow White.
s.fr: Des oiseaux et des animaux vinrent à la colline pour voir Blanche-Neige.

s.t: Years passed on the hill, and Snow White did not change.
s.fr: Les années passèrent sur la colline, et Blanche-Neige ne changea pas.

s.t: She still looked as if she were asleep.
s.fr: Elle semblait encore être endormie.

paras.summary: The dwarfs want to see Snow White again, but she does not wake, and birds and animals come to see her too; years pass, and Snow White does not change, still looking as if she were asleep.

s.t: One morning, a prince came through the forest.
s.fr: Un matin, un prince traversa la forêt.

s.t: At the hill, he saw the glass coffin.
s.fr: À la colline, il vit le cercueil de verre.

s.t: Snow White lay inside the glass coffin, asleep.
s.fr: Blanche-Neige était allongée à l’intérieur du cercueil de verre, endormie.

s.t: The prince stopped at the hill and looked at her.
s.fr: Le prince s’arrêta à la colline et la regarda.

paras.summary: One morning, a prince comes through the forest, sees the glass coffin at the hill, where Snow White lies asleep, and stops to look at her.

s.t: He asked the seven dwarfs about her.
s.fr: Il interrogea les sept nains à son sujet.

s.t: "We believe she died, but she never changes," said one dwarf.
s.fr: « Nous croyons qu’elle est morte, mais elle ne change jamais, » dit un nain.

s.t: The prince wanted to see Snow White every day.
s.fr: Le prince voulait voir Blanche-Neige chaque jour.

s.t: "Let me stay here beside her," he asked the dwarfs.
s.fr: « Laissez-moi rester ici près d’elle, » demanda-t-il aux nains.

paras.summary: He asks the seven dwarfs about her, and they say they believe she died, though she never changes; unable to look away, the prince wants to see her every day and asks to stay beside her.

s.t: The seven dwarfs saw his sad face.
s.fr: Les sept nains virent son visage triste.

s.t: They let the prince come near the glass coffin.
s.fr: Ils laissèrent le prince s’approcher du cercueil de verre.

s.t: He opened the glass coffin with care.
s.fr: Il ouvrit le cercueil de verre avec soin.

s.t: The prince kissed Snow White.
s.fr: Le prince embrassa Blanche-Neige.

paras.summary: The seven dwarfs see his sad face and let him come near the glass coffin, where birds and animals still come to the hill; he opens the coffin with care and kisses Snow White.

s.t: As the prince kissed Snow White, he raised her from the coffin.
s.fr: Quand le prince embrassa Blanche-Neige, il la souleva hors du cercueil.

s.t: The poisoned apple fell from Snow White's mouth.
s.fr: La pomme empoisonnée tomba de la bouche de Blanche-Neige.

s.t: Snow White opened her eyes at last.
s.fr: Blanche-Neige ouvrit les yeux enfin.

s.t: She saw the prince near her.
s.fr: Elle vit le prince près d’elle.

s.t: "Who are you?" Snow White asked.
s.fr: « Qui êtes-vous ? » demanda Blanche-Neige.

s.t: "You are safe with me now," said the prince.
s.fr: « Vous êtes en sécurité avec moi maintenant, » dit le prince.

s.t: He told Snow White about the glass coffin and the seven dwarfs.
s.fr: Il raconta à Blanche-Neige l’histoire du cercueil de verre et des sept nains.

paras.summary: As the prince kisses her and raises her, the poisoned apple falls from her mouth, and Snow White opens her eyes, sees him near her, and asks who he is; he tells her about the glass coffin and the seven dwarfs.

s.t: Snow White sat up and saw the seven dwarfs near her.
s.fr: Blanche-Neige se redressa et vit les sept nains près d’elle.

s.t: "You slept for many years," said one dwarf.
s.fr: « Vous avez dormi pendant de nombreuses années, » dit un nain.

paras.summary: Snow White sits up and sees the seven dwarfs near her, and one dwarf tells her she slept for many years; she thanks them as birds sing in the forest around the hill.

s.t: "Will you come to my castle with me?" the prince asked.
s.fr: « Voulez-vous venir à mon château avec moi ? » demanda le prince.

s.t: "Will you be my wife?" he asked Snow White.
s.fr: « Voulez-vous être ma femme ? » demanda-t-il à Blanche-Neige.

s.t: Snow White looked at the prince's eyes and smiled.
s.fr: Blanche-Neige regarda les yeux du prince et sourit.

s.t: "I will," said Snow White.
s.fr: « Oui, » dit Blanche-Neige.

paras.summary: The prince asks Snow White to come to his castle and be his wife, and she looks at him, smiles, and says she will.

s.t: Soon, Snow White and the prince planned their wedding.
s.fr: Bientôt, Blanche-Neige et le prince planifièrent leur mariage.

s.t: The wedding would be at the prince's big castle.
s.fr: Le mariage aurait lieu au grand château du prince.

s.t: Many guests would come from every land.
s.fr: De nombreux invités viendraient de chaque pays.

s.t: The queen learned of the wedding at the castle.
s.fr: La reine apprit le mariage au château.

s.t: She asked her mirror who was the fairest now.
s.fr: Elle demanda à son miroir qui était la plus belle maintenant.

s.t: "The prince's young wife is now the fairest," said the mirror.
s.fr: « La jeune femme du prince est maintenant la plus belle, » dit le miroir.

paras.summary: Snow White and the prince plan their wedding at his castle, with guests coming from every land, and word of it reaches the queen, who asks her mirror who is the fairest now and learns it is the prince's young wife.

s.t: The queen wanted to see this woman herself.
s.fr: La reine voulut voir cette femme elle-même.

s.t: She went to the prince's castle for the wedding.
s.fr: Elle alla au château du prince pour le mariage.

s.t: At the castle, the queen saw Snow White.
s.fr: Au château, la reine vit Blanche-Neige.

paras.summary: Wanting to see this woman herself, the queen goes to the castle for the wedding, where she sees Snow White and knows the huntsman never killed her in the forest.

s.t: Snow White knew the old woman and told the prince.
s.fr: Blanche-Neige reconnut la vieille femme et le dit au prince.

s.t: The prince learned of the tight laces, the comb, and the apple.
s.fr: Le prince apprit les lacets serrés, le peigne, et la pomme.

s.t: "You came to kill Snow White three times," the prince said.
s.fr: « Tu vins tuer Blanche-Neige trois fois, » dit le prince.

s.t: The prince made the queen go from the kingdom forever.
s.fr: Le prince fit partir la reine du royaume pour toujours.

paras.summary: Snow White knows the old woman was the queen and tells the prince, who learns of the laces, the comb, and the apple; knowing she came to kill Snow White three times, the prince makes the queen go from the kingdom forever, and she never returns.

s.t: Snow White married the prince at his castle.
s.fr: Blanche-Neige épousa le prince dans son château.

s.t: The seven dwarfs came to the wedding.
s.fr: Les sept nains vinrent au mariage.

s.t: Bells rang across the kingdom for the wedding.
s.fr: Des cloches sonnèrent dans tout le royaume pour le mariage.

paras.summary: Snow White marries the prince at his castle as the seven dwarfs come to the wedding, and bells ring across the kingdom.

s.t: Snow White thanked the seven dwarfs at the wedding.
s.fr: Blanche-Neige remercia les sept nains au mariage.

s.t: "You will always be our friend," said one dwarf.
s.fr: « Tu seras toujours notre amie », dit un nain.

s.t: Snow White promised to visit the cottage often.
s.fr: Blanche-Neige promit de visiter la chaumière souvent.

s.t: She and the prince lived on in the castle.
s.fr: Elle et le prince continuèrent à vivre dans le château.

paras.summary: Snow White thanks the seven dwarfs at the wedding, and one promises she will always be their friend; she promises to visit the cottage often, and she and the prince live on in the castle.

s.t: The glass coffin stayed on the hill in the forest.
s.fr: Le cercueil de verre resta sur la colline dans la forêt.

s.t: No one asked the mirror who was the fairest now.
s.fr: Personne ne demanda au miroir qui était la plus belle maintenant.

paras.summary: The glass coffin stays on the hill in the forest, and no one asks the mirror who is the fairest now.
